title: Do the circles for four, five and eight really cross?
description: A circle is pictured at each end of a base of eight centimetres, with radii four and five, and the distance from the end of the base to the first circle shows that the circles cross. Keeko doubts the need for circles and says the check on the lengths already shows a triangle exists.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the lengths pass the check, the circles on the base must cross, so the third corner is really there. Watch for children who think the check on the lengths alone is a proof that the triangle can be drawn.

source: Does a triangle exist with sidelengths 4 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm? Picture the circles on the longest side.
video_script.why: The child has seen that lengths failing the check make no triangle and now asks whether lengths passing the check always make one.
video_script.substitution: The base is eight centimetres, the circle at one end has radius four centimetres and the circle at the other end has radius five centimetres.
video_script.anchor: A base of eight centimetres with a circle of radius four at one end and a circle of radius five at the other
video_script.wrong_answer: the check alone already shows that a triangle exists
video_script.wrong_move: A child finds that eight is less than four plus five and stops, though the check only says a triangle may or may not exist.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, a triangle exists with sides four, five and eight centimetres.

final_answer.value: Yes, a triangle exists; the two circles cross at two places
final_answer.spoken: yes, a triangle exists with sides four, five and eight centimetres, because the two circles cross at two places

never_show: the words a triangle exists before the answer beat
maths_rules: 8 < 4 + 5 = 9, so the lengths pass the check
base AB = 8 cm; circle at A has radius 4 cm; circle at B has radius 5 cm
X is where the circle at A meets AB, so AX = 4 cm and BX = 8 - 4 = 4 cm
BX = 4 < 5 = the radius at B, so the circle at B goes beyond X, inside the circle at A
part of the circle at B is inside and part is outside the circle at A, so the circles cross at two places
video_script.design: One idea: when the check passes, the circles on the base must cross. One base and two circles; Keeko's doubt closes the video.
